text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Phone users in prime business and residential Orchard area affected by faulty telephone lines this week.

- Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto indicates proposed enhanced security cooperation between Tokyo and Washington would cover not only emergencies on the Korean Peninsula but also other potential regional flash points.
- San Jose, California bans people from sitting on sidewalks in bid to clear streets of young people and beggars.
- Former coma patient gets five O-level distinctions.
- Manufacturing output falls 5.5 percent year-on-year in February, for fourth consecutive monthly decline.
- In move raising bankers' eyebrows, property agent aggressively markets a property refinancing package on behalf of an unnamed bank.
- DBS Bank pays directors a surprisingly small Singapore $1.7 million last year.
- Nippon Credit Bank announces it will form unprecedented "business alliance" with foreign bank -- Bankers Trust New York Corp.
- Singapore investors account for almost all major hotel transactions in Asia last year, valued at more than US$1 billion.
- Ministry of Health fines two companies for placing advertisements on Internet flouting Singapore medical regulations.
- Trading company Wearnes International selling entire stake in Kuala Lumpur-listed O'Connmors unit, a move that would yield extraordinary gain of almost S$50 million.
- NatSteel and Uraco announce tie-up for electronics venture which would beef up NatSteel's soon-to-be-listed electronics subsidiary.
- Nearly half Raffles Medical Group's initial public offer alloted to small investors.
